'''Alexei Alexandrovich Starobinsky''' ({{langx|ru|Алексе́й Алекса́ндрович Староби́нский}}; 19 April 1948 – 21 December 2023) was a [[Soviet Union|Soviet]] and Russian [[Theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]] and [[Cosmology|cosmologist]]. He was a pioneer of the theory of [[Inflation (cosmology)|cosmic inflation]], for which he received the 2014 [[Kavli Prize|Kavli Prize in Astrophysics]] together with [[Alan Guth]] and [[Andrei Linde]].

Born in [[Moscow]], Starobinsky obtained a degree in physics from [[Moscow State University]] in 1972 and a doctorate in theoretical and mathematical physics from the [[Landau Institute for Theoretical Physics]] in 1975, the latter under the supervision of [[Yakov Zeldovich]]. Starobinsky remained at the Landau Institute, becoming its principal research scientist in 1997 and holding this position until his death.

While still a doctoral student, in 1973 he showed that, according to the [[uncertainty principle]], rotating black holes must emit particles. This work led to [[Stephen Hawking]] conjecturing [[Hawking radiation]]. In 1979, he became the first to propose a model of cosmic inflation, postulating what is now known as [[Starobinsky inflation]].

==Early life and education==
Alexei Alexandrovich Starobinsky was born on 19 April 1948 in [[Moscow]], in the former [[Soviet Union]], to two radio physicists.<ref name="Romantic">{{Cite web |date=September 2019 |title=A Physicist Has to Be a Romantic |url=https://www.hse.ru/en/news/research/305811947.html |access-date=31 December 2023 |publisher=[[HSE University]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231231024700/https://www.hse.ru/en/news/research/305811947.html |archive-date=31 December 2023 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="PhysToday">{{Cite web |date=19 April 2019 |title=Alexei Starobinsky |url=https://pubs.aip.org/physicstoday/online/4539/Alexei-Starobinsky |access-date=31 December 2023 |website=[[Physics Today]] |publisher=[[American Institute of Physics]]}}</ref> He went to a physics and technology high school where he graduated in 1966.<ref name="Romantic" /> He attended [[Moscow State University]], earning an [[MSc]] degree in physics in 1972.<ref name="NAS">{{Cite web |title=Alexei A. Starobinsky |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/alexei-alexandrovich-starobinsky-apy2oh/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231223133413/https://www.nasonline.org/member-directory/members/20041728.html |archive-date=23 December 2023 |access-date=24 December 2023 |url-status=live |publisher=[[National Academy of Sciences]]}}</ref> In 1975, he obtained a [[PhD]] in theoretical and mathematical physics from the [[Landau Institute for Theoretical Physics]] of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] under the supervision of [[Yakov Zeldovich]] with a thesis titled ''Quantum Effects and the Amplification of Waves in Strong Gravitational Forces''.<ref name="HSE News">{{Cite web |date=22 December 2023 |title=Academician Alexey Starobinsky Passes Away |url=https://www.hse.ru/en/our/news/881630534.html |access-date=30 December 2023 |publisher=[[HSE University]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240111122159/https://www.hse.ru/en/our/news/881630534.html |archive-date=11 January 2024 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="SFI">{{Cite web |title="У Алексея Старобинского была жажда высшей истины" |url=https://sfi.ru/sfi-today/news/u-alekseia-starobinskogo-byla-zhazhda-vysshei-istiny.html |trans-title=Aleksej Starobinskij Had a Desire for Higher Truth |access-date=21 December 2023 |script-website=ru:Свято-Филаретовский институт |website=St Philaret's Institute |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240114190720/https://sfi.ru/sfi-today/news/u-alekseia-starobinskogo-byla-zhazhda-vysshei-istiny.html |archive-date=14 January 2024 |url-status=live |date=21 December 2023 |language=ru}}</ref>

==Career==
After finishing his doctorate, he remained at the Landau Institute working as a research scientist. In 1997, he became the institute's principal research scientist, a position he held until his death. From 1990 to 1997, he headed the institute's department of gravitation and cosmology and, from 1999 to 2003, he was also the institute's deputy director.<ref name="PhysToday" /><ref name="Leopoldina">{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Alexei Starobinsky |url=https://www.leopoldina.org/en/members/list-of-members/list-of-members/member/Member/show/alexei-starobinsky/ |access-date=3 January 2024 |publisher=[[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina|Nationale Akademie der Wissenschaften Leopoldina]] |url-status=live |archive-date=3 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240103135912/https://www.leopoldina.org/en/members/list-of-members/list-of-members/member/Member/show/alexei-starobinsky/}}</ref>

Starobinsky was a visiting professor at the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École Normale Supérieure]] in 1991, the Research Center for the Early Universe at the [[University of Tokyo]] from 2000 to 2001, the [[Institut Henri Poincaré]] in 2006, the Yukawa Institute for Theoretical Physics of [[Kyoto University]] in 1994 and 2007, and [[Utrecht University]] from 2014 to 2015.<ref name="Leopoldina"/><ref name="Curriculum">{{Cite web |title=Curriculum Vitae – Alexei A. Starobinsky |url=http://www.icra.it/MG/mg15/cv/cv_starobinsky.pdf |access-date=3 January 2024 |publisher=[[International Center for Relativistic Astrophysics]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240330101939/https://www.icra.it/MG/mg15/cv/cv_starobinsky.pdf|archive-date=30 March 2024}}</ref> In 2017, he was also appointed as a part-time professor at the National Research University Higher School of Economics<ref name="HSE News"/>

Starobinsky held editorial positions in a number of journals including ''[[General Relativity and Gravitation]]'' from 1989 to 1997, the ''[[Journal of Experimental and Theoretical Physics]]'' from 1991, the ''[[International Journal of Modern Physics|International Journal of Modern Physics D]]'' from 1992 and the ''[[Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics]]'' from 2002.<ref name="Curriculum"/> He was a member of the Board of Trustees and co-chairman of the Physics and Theology roundtable at the St Philaret's Institute.<ref name="SFI"/><ref name="SFI 2">{{Cite web |title=Physicist Alexei Starobinsky Joins SFI's Board of Trustees |url=https://sfi.ru/en/sfi-today/news/akademik-starobinskii-voshiol-v-chislo-popechitelei-sfi.html |access-date=11 June 2024 |script-website=ru:Свято-Филаретовский институт |website=St Philaret's Institute |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221003184125/https://sfi.ru/en/sfi-today/news/akademik-starobinskii-voshiol-v-chislo-popechitelei-sfi.html |archive-date=3 October 2022 |url-status=live |date=7 July 2023}}</ref>

==Research==
[[File:CMB Timeline300 no WMAP.jpg|thumb|upright=1.5|Timeline of the universe's evolution over 13.77 billion years. It is thought that the "inflationary epoch" lasted around <math>10^{-32}</math> seconds and that during this period the universe expanded by a factor of at least <math>10^{25}</math>.{{sfn|Gribbin|1996|p=220}}{{sfn|Guth|1997|p=14}}]]

Starobinsky's research commenced while he was still a student in the early 1970s with the study of particle creation in the early universe alongside Zeldovich. In 1973, building on Zeldovich's prior research, he showed that, according to the [[uncertainty principle]], rotating black holes must emit particles.{{sfn|Starobinsky|Zel'dovich|1971}}{{sfn|Starobinsky|Churilov|1973}} They were visited in Moscow by [[Stephen Hawking]], who was spurred to find a precise mathematical treatment for this phenomenon.{{sfn|Ferguson|2011|p=86}} He would later conjecture that all black holes (not just rotating ones) emit energetic particles, a theoretical effect known today as [[Hawking radiation]].{{efn|Hawking radiation has not yet been directly observed or proven experimentally. It is predicted to be incredibly faint and below the detecting ability of the current best telescopes.}}{{Sfn|White|Gribbin|2002|p=146}}{{sfn|Hawking|1974}}

Subsequently, Starobinsky shifted his focus to cosmology. He began investigating the early universe and the [[Big Bang]], attempting to use quantum mechanics and general relativity to understand how an expanding universe may have formed. In 1979, he became the first to propose a model for how the early universe could have gone through an extremely rapid period of exponential expansion.<ref name="Kavli Prize">{{Cite web |last=Clery |first=Daniel |date=2014 |title=Pioneering the theory of cosmic inflation |url=https://www.kavliprize.org/prizes/astrophysics/2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230111124736/https://www.kavliprize.org/prizes/astrophysics/2014 |archive-date=11 January 2023 |url-status=live |access-date=13 January 2024 |website=[[Kavli Prize]] |publisher=[[Kavli Foundation (United States)|Kavli Foundation]]}}</ref>{{sfn|Gribbin|1996|p=221}} His model, now known as [[Starobinsky inflation]],{{efn|At the time, because the term 'inflation' had not yet been coined, the model was known just as the <em>Starobinsky model</em>.{{sfn|Gribbin|1996|p=221}}}} postulates that the expansion was driven by [[quantum gravity]] effects.{{sfn|Gribbin|1996|p=221}} Starobinsky also found that this expansion would have produced [[gravitational wave]]s detectable today as a [[Gravitational wave background|background]].{{sfn|Starobinsky|1979}} Despite its significance, his work remained unknown outside of the Soviet Union.{{sfn|Gribbin|1996|p=221}}{{sfn|Guth|1997|p=229}} Around the same period, [[Alan Guth]] independently proposed a theory of exponential expansion, which he termed '[[Inflation (cosmology)|inflation]]', to tackle the [[Horizon problem|horizon]], [[Flatness problem|flatness]] and [[magnetic monopole]] problems with the Big Bang.<ref name="Kavli Prize"/><ref name="Gruber Prize">{{Cite web |last=Hreha |first=Sarah |date=7 November 2013 |title=2013 Gruber Cosmology Prize Press Release |url=https://gruber.yale.edu/press/2013-gruber-cosmology-prize-press-release |access-date=13 January 2024 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240112210157/https://gruber.yale.edu/press/2013-gruber-cosmology-prize-press-release |archive-date=12 January 2024 |publisher=[[Gruber Foundation]] |publication-place=New Haven}}</ref> The shortcomings with Guth's theory were successfully fixed by [[Andrei Linde]] in 1981.{{sfn|Gribbin|1996|pp=221&ndash;222}}

The Starobinsky model of inflation implied that [[quantum fluctuation]]s, random disturbances of a point in space, would have been stretched beyond the quantum scale by the exponential expansion of the universe.<ref>{{Cite web |last=da Silva |first=Wilson |author-link1 = Wilson da Silva |date=2 March 2015 |title=The physicist who inflated the Universe |url=https://cosmosmagazine.com/space/the-physicist-who-inflated-the-universe/ |access-date=13 January 2024 |url-status=live |archive-date=13 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240113020038/https://cosmosmagazine.com/space/the-physicist-who-inflated-the-universe/ |website=[[Cosmos (Australian magazine)|Cosmos]] |language=en-AU}}</ref> [[Viatcheslav Mukhanov]] and [[Gennady Chibisov]] proposed that these quantum fluctuations eventually resulted in the largest structures in the universe.{{sfn|Mukhanov|Chibisov|1981}} Their predictions have been matched by observations of the cosmic microwave background.<ref name="Gruber Prize"/>

==Personal life and politics==
Starobinsky's father died when he was two years old.<ref name="Romantic" /> In February 2022, he signed an open letter by Russian scientists condemning the [[Russian invasion of Ukraine]].<ref>{{cite web |date=24 February 2022 |script-title=ru:Открытое письмо российских учёных и научных журналистов против войны с Украиной |trans-title=Open letter of Russian scientists and science journalists against the war in Ukraine |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240510111403/https://t-invariant.org/2022/02/we-are-against-war/ |archive-date=10 May 2024 |url=https://t-invariant.org/2022/02/we-are-against-war/ |access-date=2 April 2022 |website=T-Invariant |language=ru |script-website=ru:Т-инвариант}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Stern |first=Boris |date=30 March 2022 |title="The war against Ukraine is unjust and senseless": Russian scientists courageously condemn the invasion |url=https://theins.info/en/opinion/boris-stern/249819 |access-date=31 December 2023 |website=[[The Insider (website)|The Insider]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231231023158/https://theins.info/en/opinion/boris-stern/249819 |archive-date=31 December 2023}}</ref> Starobinsky died on 21 December 2023 at the age of 75.<ref name="SFI"/> He is buried in the [[Novodevichy Cemetery]] in [[Moscow]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 March 2024 |title=СТАРОБИНСКИЙ Алексей Александрович (1948 – 2023) |url=https://moscow-tombs.ru/by-years/starobinsky_aa/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240404140235/https://moscow-tombs.ru/by-years/starobinsky_aa/ |archive-date=4 April 2024 |access-date=15 April 2024 |website=Moscow-Tombs |script-website=ru:Московские могилы |language=ru}}</ref>

==Honors and awards==
Starobinsky received the [[Medal "For Labour Valour"|Medal For Labour Valour]] of the Soviet Union in 1986 and the second class [[Order "For Merit to the Fatherland"|Order For Merit to the Fatherland]] in 2009.<ref name="HSE News"/>

Starobinsky was awarded the 1996 [[Friedmann Prize]] for his work on the inflationary stage of the universe and its observational manifestations.<ref name="RAS">{{cite web |title=Премия имени А.А. Фридмана |trans-title=A. A. Friedmann Prize |url=http://www.ras.ru/win/db/award_dsc.asp?P=id-78.ln-ru |access-date=3 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611010945/https://www.ras.ru/win/db/award_dsc.asp?P=id-78.ln-ru |url-status=live |archive-date=11 June 2023 |publisher=[[Russian Academy of Sciences]] |language=ru}}</ref> He and Mukhanov were joint recipients of the 2009 [[Tomalla Foundation|Tomalla Prize]] for their contributions to cosmological inflation, with Starobinsky specifically recognised for his calculations of the gravitational radiation emitted during the inflationary epoch of the universe.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tomalla Foundation Prize Holders |url=http://www.tomalla.ch/prize_winner.htm |access-date=23 December 2023 |publisher=[[Tomalla Foundation]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240501085544/http://www.tomalla.ch/prize_winner.htm |archive-date=1 May 2024}}</ref> He received the [[Oskar Klein Memorial Lecture|Oskar Klein Medal]] in 2010.<ref name="PhysToday" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Freeland |first=Emily E. |date=30 May 2023 |title=Previous Oskar Klein Memorial Lectures |url=https://www.su.se/cmlink/2.48708/research/memorial-lecture/earlier-lectures |access-date=2 January 2024 |url-status=live |archive-date=2 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240102021721/https://www.su.se/cmlink/2.48708/research/memorial-lecture/earlier-lectures |publisher=[[Stockholm University]]}}</ref> Starobinsky and Mukhanov were also co-recipients of the Amaldi Medal from the [[Italian Society for General Relativity and Gravitation]] in 2012 and the [[Gruber Prize in Cosmology]] in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |url-status=live |archive-date=3 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240203155025/https://www.sigrav.org/en/awards/amaldi_medal/ |title=The Amaldi Medal |url=https://www.sigrav.org/en/awards/amaldi_medal/ |access-date=2 January 2024 |publisher=[[Italian Society for General Relativity and Gravitation]] |language=en}}</ref><ref name="IAU Gruber">{{Cite Universe's Earliest Moments |url=https://www.iau.org/news/pressreleases/detail/iau1304/|access-date=2 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230713123655/https://www.iau.org/news/pressreleases/detail/iau1304/ |url-status=live |archive-date=13 July 2023 |publisher=[[International Astronomical Prize|Kavli Prize in Astrophysics]] by the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]] for his pioneering contributions to the theory of cosmic inflation.<ref name="AAAS">{{Cite news |last=Bhattacharjee |first=Yudhijit |date=29 May 2014 |title=Nine Scientists Share Three Kavli Prizes |work=ScienceInsider Starobinsky was elected a correspondent member of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] in 1997 before becoming a full member in 2011.<ref name="NAS" /> He was also an elected member of the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]], the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters and the [[National Academy of Sciences|United States National Academy of Science]] as well as a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref name="Leopoldina" /><ref name="US NAS">{{Cite web |date=18 May 2017 |title=Alexei Starobinsky, Professor in Faculty of Physics, Elected Foreign Associate at U.S. National Academy of Sciences |url=https://www.hse.ru/en/news/206073955.html |publisher=[[HSE University]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240112214740/https://www.hse.ru/en/news/206073955.html |url-status=live |archive-date=12 January 2024}}</ref>
